--- page 1 ---
Cover page: OCHA Anticipatory Action Framework, "Bangladesh Cyclones – 2023." Approved by RC on 11/9/2023 (revision approved 13/05/2024); endorsed by USG/ERC on 23/12/2023 (revision endorsed 17/05/2024). Table of contents listing sections 1-7 (Introduction, Model, Delivery, Money/CERF, Learning, Final provisions, Annexes) with page numbers.

--- page 2 ---
Executive summary: coordinated AA framework for cyclones in Bangladesh, initiated Jan 2023, led by RC, funded via CERF plus partner co-financing. Bulleted "Current structure and activation protocol": readiness activation 3-5 days before landfall (full CERF funding disbursed but only readiness activities allowed); action activation triggers full implementation with no further approval; if action trigger not preceded by readiness trigger, disbursement and implementation happen simultaneously.

--- page 3 ---
Flowchart "Framework structure and activation protocol": timeline axis "Time ahead of expected landfall" from 5 days lead time down to landfall. Readiness phase (3-5 days): continuous monitoring of cyclone forecasts → if readiness criteria met → readiness activation notification email to partners → based on pre-approved budgets → full CERF funding disbursed to partners. At 3 days lead time, Action phase (48-72 hours): continuous monitoring → if action activation criteria met → activation notification sent to partners → no further approval required → full implementation of AA activities (if action trigger not preceded by readiness trigger, funding released at same time). Below 48 hours lead time: "No activation possible" — box states no activation of the framework if forecast lead time is less than 48 hours, down to landfall.

--- page 4 ---
Narrative text (Introduction section): background on OCHA/RC request Jan 2023 to expand AA to cyclones and monsoon floods; history of BDRCS/WFP piloting AA in 2015/2017/2019; AA Technical Working Group under HCTT; linked to EW4All initiative. No distinct figure.

--- page 5 ---
Narrative text (Risk/Hazard, Anticipatory Action, Prior AA in Bangladesh sections). Key figures stated in text: severe cyclone hits Bangladesh every ~3 years (MoEF); BMD data show 10 cyclones impacted coastal districts 1991-2023, 6 tropical cyclones with wind speed >118 km/h formed in Bay of Bengal. Describes 3 core elements of AA frameworks (model/delivery/money) and prior BDRCS/WFP pilots (2015, 2017, 2019) and 2020 monsoon flood activation. No distinct figure.

--- page 6 ---
Narrative text: 2020 pilot activation details (4 July 2020 trigger, >220,000 people assisted via WFP/FAO/UNFPA); 2021 pilot framework for monsoon floods (5 districts: Bogura, Gaibandha, Kurigram, Jamalpur, Sirajganj); Overarching framework/core principles (RC-led, CERF, HCTT/AA-TWG coordination); start of Section 2 "The Model: Forecast and Triggers" — Forecast (BMD/IMD/ECMWF/GFS/JTWC sources, cyclone season Apr-Jun & Oct-Nov) and Trigger (intro sentence). No distinct figure.

--- page 7 ---
Narrative text (Trigger section detail): defines trigger as 1-in-5-year return period ≥118 km/h wind speed (25% household asset damage). Two-stage trigger system: Stage I Readiness (CERF funding release) — BMD Signal 1+ warning with 3-5 day lead time AND ≥2 of 5 models (BMD/IMD/ECMWF/GFS/JTWC) forecasting ≥118 km/h in coastal districts, OR ≥2 models alone with 3-5 day lead time. Stage II Action (implementation start) — BMD Signal 5+ with 48-72 hour lead time AND ≥2 models forecasting ≥118 km/h, OR ≥2 models alone with 48-72 hour lead time. Cutoff for activation: 48 hours ahead of landfall (safety reasons); shorter lead times managed manually by RC. Monitoring steps: named monitoring team (Ahmadul Hassan, Pauline Ndirangu, Leonardo Milano) and 4-step analysis process. Start of "Roles and responsibilities" table (Who/What/How/When) with first row: AA Working Group - Cyclone focal point/Monitoring team.

--- page 8 ---
Continuation of Roles and responsibilities table: AA Working Group communicates trigger status to HCTT/RC/agencies via email and WhatsApp (with intervention map); CERF Secretariat sends approval letters to agencies when readiness/action trigger reached; RC and MoDMR can pause activation in outlier cases (track would result in minimal impact). Below table, text on pausing activation. "Challenges and potential improvements" bullets: need for impact-based forecasting, short lead times, and other untargeted hazards (rainfall, storm surge, monsoon floods).

--- page 9 ---
Section 3 "The Delivery: Anticipatory Action Plan" — Overview narrative on humanitarian impacts (livelihood/asset loss, GBV risk, livestock mortality). Table: district ranking by INFORM Risk analysis and cyclone frequency (wind >118km/h, Cat.1), 1977-2023, used to select 5 of 8 sea-facing districts. Columns: Rank, Districts, INFORM Natural Hazard, INFORM Vulnerability, Frequency Exceeding Wind Speed 118km/h, Score. Values: 1 Satkhira 6.9/5.5/0.1304/4.95; 2 Patuakhali 5.6/6.7/0.1304/4.89; 3 Bhola 5.0/5.8/0.1522/4.41; 4 Noakhali 5.9/5.6/0.1304/4.31; 5 Barguna 7.2/6.4/0.0870/4.01; 6 Khulna 6.0/5.9/0.0870/3.08; 7 Pirojpur 5.4/6.1/0.0870/2.86; 8 Bagerhat 6.0/6.5/0.0652/2.54. Start of FAO interventions section (objectives: protect livelihood assets).

--- page 10 ---
FAO-led AA actions: targets 10,000 farming households in Satkhira, Barguna, Patuakhali, Noakhali (+25,000 households with early warning). Readiness phase: beneficiary registration, EWM development, government sensitisation. Action phase: EWM dissemination, distribution of water/air-proof seed/food/water storage silos, nutrient-enriched animal feed (50kg/household), Cash+ grants, impact assessment. UNFPA interventions (objectives: GBV/SRH mitigation) — targets 7,000 at-risk women/girls (1,000 pregnant, 200 trans women) in Patuakhali and Noakhali: 3,000 dignity kits (incl. 200 for trans women), 3,000 MHM kits, 1,000 baby kits, cash for transport for 6,000 women. UNICEF objectives intro: multi-sectoral WASH/Education/Cash/Child Protection/CCE across all 5 districts (Bhola, Barguna, Patuakhali, Noakhali, Satkhira).

--- page 11 ---
UNICEF-led AA actions: targets up to 300,000 vulnerable community members across 5 districts — WASH services, uninterrupted education, unconditional cash (BDT 5,000 to 2,500 households targeting pregnant/lactating mothers with children 0-4), CCE/forecast contextualization, government capacity strengthening. WFP interventions (objectives: preparedness & food assistance) — targets 45,000 households (poor/vulnerable) in Khulna, Satkhira, Patuakhali, Barguna, Bhola; pre-verified bKash accounts; one-off unconditional cash transfer BDT 5,000 (US$42, =75% of Minimum Expenditure Basket for 5-person household) via bKash before cyclone; post-cyclone cash support described further on next page.

--- page 12 ---
Continuation of WFP actions: post-cyclone cash support — (A) 28,650 families receive BDT 3,000 (US$27) for household repairs; (B) 28,650 families receive BDT 1,500 (US$14) for dry food/water jerry cans. Plus cyclone early warning dissemination with CPP volunteers. Section 4 "The Money: CERF" — CERF envelope of US$7.5M for AA; same pool used for both cyclone (Oct-Dec, Apr-Jun) and riverine flood (Jun-Oct) triggers, not guaranteed for both. Table "Financing overview": Agency/Funding Requirement (US$): FAO 782,349; UNFPA 448,510; UNICEF 2,299,962; WFP 3,900,000; Total 7,430,821.

--- page 13 ---
Table "Co funding": Agency / Contingency Budget for AA implementation (USD) / Funding mechanism / Remarks. BDRCS 551,464 (499,000 CHF) - DREF - Verified; WFP 3,000,000 - ECHO, Internal funds - Verified; Care Int'l 275,000 - Start Fund and ECHO - needs verification; Christian Aid 115,000 - Internal Funding - Approx; Concern Worldwide 55,000 - Internal Funding - Approx; STEP Consortium 35,000 - ECHO; UNFPA 806,330 - Japan & DFAT Regional Prepositioning Initiative - supports FbAA preparedness; START Network 755,000 - Start Fund; Islamic Relief 45,000 - Internal Funding; FAO 179,000 - SFERA. Below: CERF section — ERC allocated US$7.5M; three conditions for CERF disbursement (RC endorsement, ERC pre-approval, activation within 2 years).

--- page 14 ---
Narrative text: CERF disbursement is guaranteed/no-regrets once trigger reached; readiness vs action funding portions defined in advance; pre-arranged CERF funding doesn't preclude additional CERF for other needs. "Challenges" bullets: start-up/build costs of collective AA not covered by pooled funds; limited preparedness/prepositioning funding; AA may not cover all affected beyond targeted scope. Section 5 "The Learning": ad hoc MEAL committee convened by OCHA; pre-identified learning areas begin (Timing: did intervention timing relative to landfall matter?). No distinct figure.

--- page 15 ---
Continuation of Learning-area bullets: Joint targeting, Early warning, Localisation, Partnership, Pre-crisis survey, Actions, Effectiveness, AAP (accountability to affected populations). Monitoring & Evaluation section (agency M&E systems, shared with OCHA, coordinated questionnaires). Independent Evaluation section (agencies agree to participate, ad hoc committee oversees). Section 6 "Final provisions" / Advocacy and Public Communications (joint press release, shared visuals/impact stories). No distinct figure beyond text.

--- page 16 ---
Section 7 Annexes, Annex 1 – Historical Analysis. Table 1: "Historical data on cyclone impact on coastal areas of Bangladesh" (used for return-period calc against 118 km/h wind speed). Columns: Year, Name, Wind speed (km/h), Storm surge height (m), Affected population, Affected houses (fully damaged), Loss of life, Livestock. Key rows: 1991 Bob 1 – 250 km/h, 6.5m surge, 15,000,000 affected, 854,399 houses, 138,882 deaths, 700,000 livestock; 2007 Sidr – 223 km/h, 4.57m, 6,737,815 affected, 564,967 houses, >10,000 deaths, 382,000 livestock; 2009 Aila – 120 km/h, 3.05m, 3.9M affected, 243,000 houses, 190 deaths; 2015 Komen – 65 km/h; 2016 Roanu – 90 km/h, 24 deaths; 2017 Mora – 146 km/h, 7 deaths; 2019 Fani – 88 km/h, 17 deaths, 175 livestock; 2019 Bulbul – 140 km/h, 25 deaths; 2020 Amphan – 151 km/h, 3-5m surge, 2.6M affected, 55,667 houses, 26 deaths; 2021 Yaas – 150 km/h, 9 deaths; 2022 Sitrang – 88 km/h, 35 deaths; 2023 Mocha – 145 km/h, 0.75M affected, 17,000 houses, 0 deaths.

--- page 17 ---
Map 1: "Map of cyclone hit frequency" (used for district selection). Choropleth map of Bangladesh districts/upazilas colored by frequency of cyclone events (1977-2023, wind speed >118 km/h, Cat.1+), legend scale 2 (lightest) to 7 (darkest, dark red/brown). Highest frequency (6-7, dark red/brown) concentrated in southern coastal districts: Satkhira, Patuakhali, Bhola, Barguna, and Chittagong/Cox's Bazar/Bandarban area. A dashed vertical line labeled "consider in analysis" separates the western/central coastal districts (Satkhira through Noakhali/Feni, considered in this framework) from the eastern Chittagong Hill Tracts area (Khagrachari, Parbattya Chattagram, Cox's Bazar) which appear excluded from consideration despite high frequency.

--- page 18 ---
Graph 1: "Wind speed reduction factor model in respect to distance" — two scatter/trend charts. Left: Cyclone Amphan (2020), x-axis Distance from Landfall (km, 0-600), y-axis Reduction factor (0-1), fitted curve y=0.9807e^-0.003x, R²=0.7695, factor drops from ~1.0 near landfall to ~0.2 at 500km. Right: Cyclone Mocha (2023), x-axis Distance in km (0-160), y-axis Reduction Factor (0-1.00), fitted curve y=1.0666e^-0.007x, R²=0.9678, factor drops from ~0.9 to ~0.35 at 150km. Graph 2: "HH asset damage curve with respect to wind speed differentiated by wall type" — two line charts (Central Coastal Zone and Western Coastal Zone), x-axis Wind Speed (km/hr, 0-250), y-axis Damage Percent (0-100), comparing Kacha (tin roof and wall, blue) vs Semi-Pucca (tin roof and brick wall, orange); Kacha shows higher damage than Semi-Pucca at same wind speed in both zones, reaching ~90-100% damage by 150-225 km/hr. Table 2: "Impacts (damage percentage) on rural houses for windspeed of 118 km/h": Central zone – Semi Pucca 30%, Kacha 40%, weighted avg 30%; Western zone – Semi Pucca 20%, Kacha 45%, weighted avg 25% (based on BDRCS/GRC survey of ~200 households). Table 3 (start): "Cyclone forecast models" — BMD row: Windspeed/Storm Surge content, lead time DD 48hr/CS 30hr, skill good when storm 1,000km from coast.

--- page 19 ---
Continuation of Table 3 "Cyclone forecast models": IMD (track+wind+tentative surge, DD 48-120hr/SCS 48hr+, good after CS formation but surge needs improvement), ECMWF (wind & storm surge, 10 days, good after DD formation), GFS (wind & storm surge, 10 days, good after D/DD formation), JTWC (track+wind+tentative surge, after DD formation, good after CS formation). Table: "Performance of forecast models" — forecast errors by organization/model at 24/48/72 hour lead times. Key rows: BMD track error 60-80/80-100/100-120 km, intensity error 15-20/20-30/20-40 km/hr, landfall time error 1-2/3-4/4-6 hr; RSMC-IMD track 65/90/115 km; JTWC track 24/54/80 km, intensity 13.7/12.9/14.1 km/hr; ECMWF track 78/103/154 km; NCEP-GFS track 78/115/170 km. Text notes track forecast error beyond 48hrs is very high, so usable only for readiness not activation.

Annex 3 – Trigger Messages: template emails. "[action trigger]" email — subject "Activation Trigger Reached," 48-hour forecasts indicate wind speeds expected to exceed 125 km/h; all activities commence.
